spellbook.finance/limitations: not_found means no exact identifier or within-window buyer/street match was found. Exact order IDs, labels, tracking numbers and session IDs search shipped history. Buyer/street matching checks only the 2,000 most recent distinct order/address facts, so an older fuzzy match can be outside coverage. An order SpellBook Finance never pulled or never marked shipped is absent.

An exact match on an order id, order label, tracking number or session id hides partial buyer matches for that identifier. ambiguous means more than one order matched, so confirm the order with the person before recording.
This read carries no carrier scan state. SpellBook Finance does not detect a return to sender from USPS scans, so a package can be back with the seller while returnCase is null.
A stored postal status can lag a return. One returned letter still read in_transit after it was back with the seller, so trust the person over that status.

destinationSummary is null when the pull lines carry no buyer address, which is usual for TCGplayer orders. missingFields then names results[].matches[].destinationSummary. spellbook_returned_package_reship_prepare then reads the address from the packing slip linked to the order.

A TCGplayer pull sheet can hold several orders. Each match counts only its exact order lines. Pass that match's externalOrderId with its sessionId to spellbook_returned_package_record. Separate orders on the same sheet get separate cases.

Lookup matches omit card names to keep maximum batches bounded. Counts and exact order identity remain available here; after recording the return, spellbook_returned_package_case returns the original contents.
Delegated calls require the workspace owner role.

annotations.title: Look up a shipped order and its return

description: Find shipped orders by marketplace order id, order label, tracking number, pull session id, or part of a buyer name or street line, and read each exact order's shipment facts and newest return case. Use it when a package came back before calling spellbook_returned_package_record. A multi-order pull sheet returns separate exact-order matches, each with its own returnCase. Use externalOrderId to record one selected order from a shared sheet. Each match carries sessionId, marketplace, externalOrderId, buyerName, shippedAt, trackingNumber, destinationSummary, packed and unresolved line counts, and returnCase. Card names are omitted to keep maximum batch responses bounded. Returns one row per identifier with status matched, ambiguous or not_found, plus missingFields. After recording a returned order, read its exact contents with spellbook_returned_package_case and find its task in spellbook_returned_package_work.

identifiers.description: Up to 50 values to look up, each a marketplace order id, order label, tracking number, pull session id, or part of a buyer name or street line. Required, at least one.

workspaceId.description: The workspace that shipped the orders, from spellbook_workspaces_list. Required.
